(c)Private Market Sector Housing
Available on the private market (excluding subsidized housing), are a number of dwelling units for both rental and purchase. These units are diverse in both type and character. The total private housing stock of the City and the SMSA prior to the storm was approximately 156,148 dwelling units.
These are separated into 107,537 units of owner occupied, 44,097 units of renter occupied, and 4,514 vacant units. These figures indicate a vacancy rate of 4.2 percent and an ownership rate of 41 percent for the area. These percentages and figures have changed somewhat as a result of the Storm. Unfortunately, there are no exact figures due to the complexity of the activities being continually carried on to restore the housing stock to its original status prior to the Storm. It is estimated that approximately 2,000 dwelling units were damaged by the flooding in the City of Harrisburg. Of this number, 915 structures within the project area received damage of some type and that 10 dwelling units were destroyed or had to be razed shortly after the flooding occurred. At present, twelve families are known to be displaced from the project and are relocated in public or emergency housing as a result of the flooding. A great many others were displaced but have found other temporary housing. Estimated at approximately 200, these individuals are slowly repairing their houses and returning to the area.
Census figures indicate that prior to the storm, the median rent paid in the City of Harrisburg was rather low -- $85 per month per unit, and that the median value per dwelling unit, for owner occupied properties, amounted to approximately $9,460. This is probably typical of the project area.
Non-whites occupied 6,177 of the dwelling units in the City. About 43,7 recent of the dwelling units in which non-whites lived were owner occupied and 56.3 percent were renter occupied.
(7) City Sewage and Water Systems
(a) Storm and Sanitary Sewers
The City's sewage is processed by a treatment plant immediately adjacent to the southernmost boundary of the City on the eastern bank of the Susquehanna River.
